messages:
emma (Partnerships): Quick sync — vendor call this Thurs. Need clarity on how they want reserved buckets split vs spot, plus how marketplace fees apply when we auto-convert. TLDR: finance + ops input required.
raj (Finance): Do we have the partner's preferred split matrix yet? e.g., 70/30 reserved/spot or sliding by quarter?
sophie (Sales): They sketched 60/40 in the deck but said 'we can be flexible for onboarding credits.' not binding.
michael (SRE): From infra side, important to know preemptible eviction cadence. If spot eviction >= 15% we'll need a dampening policy to avoid sudden cost spikes.
emma (Partnerships): Agree. Can we codify a dampening rule: if spot eviction spikes >10% over a rolling week, automatically throttle conversions to reserved until stability?
raj (Finance): That makes sense. Also need to calculate marketplace fee pass-through. If partner charges marketplace fee on reserved SKU but not on ephemeral, unit economics change. Can we get fee granularity per SKU?
emma (Partnerships): Asked partner for CSV with columns: sku, region, reserved_price_monthly, spot_price_hourly, marketplace_fee_pct, eviction_rate_estimate. Asked for by EOD Wed.
sophie (Sales): I'll nudge them. Also: what about onboarding credits — do we apply them only to reserved usage or to all usage? Partner prefers applying to reserved only. Thoughts?
julia (Legal): If credits only cover reserved, need explicit contract clause and invoice line items. I'll draft a short addendum.
michael (SRE): Practical ops note: when we convert spot -> reserved policy runs, we should atomically update routing rules to avoid double-charging in billing pipeline. Ops bot can trigger a flag.
ops-bot: deploy-hook: feature-toggle "partner-spot-damping" created in staging. Use /ops deploy to push.
raj (Finance): For cost modeling I propose we simulate 3 scenarios: conservative (40% reserved), baseline (60% reserved), aggressive (80% reserved) and include marketplace fee at 0%, 5%, 10%. I'll run Monte Carlo for eviction volatility.
emma (Partnerships): Perfect. Can you deliver a CSV of modeled unit costs by SKU + scenario by Thu noon?
raj (Finance): Yes — will include columns: sku, scenario, reserved_util_monthly, spot_util_monthly, avg_unit_cost_usd, marketplace_fee_usd, notes.
sophie (Sales): Sales ask: we need an example ARR impact statement for partners so AE can pitch. Short one-pager please.
emma (Partnerships): I'll draft the one-pager once modelling is in.
julia (Legal): Heads-up — partner requested a clause for 'graceful eviction notice' of 24 hrs on reserved conversions. That's unusual; will push back to 72 hrs minimum.
michael (SRE): 72 hrs seems reasonable operationally. Also: request partner to provide eviction metrics per region (CSV sample) so we can feed autoscaler. Sample snippet I asked for:```sku,region,eviction_rate_30d,median_downtime_minutes,preemptible_window```
emma (Partnerships): Noted. I'll add those fields to the CSV ask.
sophie (Sales): If partner agrees to >=72 hrs notice, sales will promote stronger enterprise pitch. :thumbsup:
raj (Finance): One more: how do we handle refunds or crediting when partner fails to meet committed reserved capacity? Need SLA credit language.
julia (Legal): I'll draft a short SLA credit template and loop in partner counsel.
emma (Partnerships): OK action items: 1) Emma: finalize CSV spec and send to partner by EOD Wed. 2) Raj: Monte Carlo scenarios by Thu noon. 3) Michael: prepare ops gating checklist and ensure deploy hook safe. 4) Julia: draft addendum + SLA credit template. 5) Sophie: sales one-pager draft after Raj's model.
emma (Partnerships): Anyone else?
michael (SRE): One small ask — include a sample timeframe for capacity ramp (weeks to full commit). Helps autoscaler.
emma (Partnerships): Good catch — will add that field to the CSV: commit_weeks_to_full.
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: "partner-csv-deadline" on 2183952000 (Wed 9am UTC).
emma (Partnerships): Thanks all. I'll post the final CSV template here when sent. :eyes:
